title: Peculiar Dust Emission within the Orion Molecular Cloud
question: What is the origin of the flattened spectral energy distribution (SED) slope at wavelengths > 2 mm toward protostellar cores in the OMC 2/3 complex on core and envelope scales (~0.02 - 0.08 pc)?

data.sensitivity: 1.1, 1.5, 1.2, 1.7 mJy beam^-1 (1.2x higher for MMS9 and NW167)

what.value: Protostellar classifications, ALMA 0.87 mm (338.5 GHz) disk fluxes and masses, and VLA 9 mm disk masses

evidence.quote: Protostellar classifications (column 4) and disk masses (columns 5 and 6) are taken from (cite: Tobin2020), which presents ALMA 0.87 mm and VLA 9 mm observations.
$S_{disk}$ flux values are measured at 0.87 mm (338.5 GHz) and represent the sum of all disks in the targets from (cite: Tobin2020).

what.value: Envelope masses from the Herschel Orion Protostellar Survey (HOPS)

evidence.quote: The envelope masses (column 7) are taken from the Herschel Orion Protostellar Survey (cite: Furlan2016).

what.value: Single-dish modified blackbody fits and dust opacity indices (beta-SD) from Herschel and IRAM 30 m (0.16 - 2 mm) data

evidence.quote: the best-fit modified black body function obtained using single-dish data ($\beta$-SD; solid lines) from (cite: Sadavoy2016) using data from Herschel and IRAM (0.16 – 2 mm).
$\beta$-SD is measured using a modified black-body fit to single-dish data only from (cite: Sadavoy2016).

what.value: 90 GHz (3.3 mm) GBT MUSTANG continuum data

evidence.quote: Moreover, we find excellent agreement between the NOEMA data and the 90 GHz (3.3 mm) data obtained from MUSTANG presented by (cite: Schnee2014).

what.value: Estimated free-free emission fractions at 32.9 GHz and spectral indices between 32.9, 246.2, and 333 GHz for FIR2 and MMS9

evidence.quote: Table [\[FF\]](#FF) displays their estimated free-free emission fractions at 32.9 GHz based on the analysis of (cite: Bouvier2021).

recipe.goal: Match spatial scales and angular resolution between ALMA-ACA and NOEMA continuum images
recipe.method: Image ALMA-ACA sidebands with a uv > 5 klambda cutoff to match the minimum baseline of NOEMA, then smooth each paired ALMA and NOEMA image by the synthesized beam of the other.
key_parameters: Baseband pairings: LSB-O with Band 4-Low, LSB-I with Band 4-High, USB-I with Band 5-Low, USB-O with Band 5-High

recipe.goal: Extract integrated source fluxes and sizes across all 8 frequency bands
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian functions plus a free constant background level in the image plane using CASA imfit.
key_parameters: NOEMA box size: 30x30 pixels; ALMA box size: about 50x50 pixels; dooff = True
assumptions: 2D Gaussian source morphology with constant local background

recipe.goal: Fit SED spectral index (alpha) and dust opacity index (beta) for NOEMA and ALMA separately
recipe.method: Fit simple power-law models S_nu = A * nu^alpha to the NOEMA (4 bands) and ALMA-ACA (4 bands) fluxes separately using MCMC (emcee), and perform a 5000-sample Monte Carlo simulation to include 10% correlated Band 4 and Band 5 flux calibration uncertainties.
key_parameters: 32 walkers, uniform prior -5.0 < alpha < 5.0, 5000 Monte Carlo samples with Gaussian(mean=1, std=0.1) for ALMA calibration error
assumptions: Rayleigh-Jeans approximation: alpha = 2 + beta, with power-law dust opacity kappa_nu propto nu^beta

recipe.goal: Estimate fraction of NOEMA and ALMA continuum flux arising from embedded protostellar disks
recipe.method: Sum 338.5 GHz (0.87 mm) disk fluxes within the NOEMA beam from Tobin et al. (2020) and extrapolate to NOEMA and ALMA frequencies using a power law S_nu propto nu^alpha with alpha = 2 and alpha = 3.
key_parameters: Reference frequency = 338.5 GHz; assumed disk spectral indices alpha = 2 (beta = 0) and alpha = 3 (beta = 1)
assumptions: 340 GHz high-resolution (40 au) ALMA observations filter out core and envelope emission and trace only disk emission, which follows a constant power law with alpha between 2 and 3.

answer_key.quantity: Median dust opacity index beta-NOEMA across sample

evidence.quote: The median $\beta$ indices are 0.74, 0.68, and 1.8 for the NOEMA, ALMA, and single-dish data, respectively

answer_key.quantity: Median dust opacity index beta-ALMA across sample

evidence.quote: The median $\beta$ indices are 0.74, 0.68, and 1.8 for the NOEMA, ALMA, and single-dish data, respectively

score_reason: The ALMA project code, calibrators, self-calibration intervals, uv-cut, robust weighting, beam pairing, source extraction task (imfit with dooff=True), intermediate extracted fluxes (Table 3), and MCMC/MC fitting procedure are all clearly reported; however, NOEMA visibilities are less accessible, and exact ALMA imaging parameters (cell size, clean thresholds, line-free channel masks) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA-ACA dataset (2017.1.00357.S) is public in the ALMA archive, the imaging and source extraction recipe is straightforward, and all intermediate fluxes and final ALMA spectral indices (alpha-ALMA and beta-ALMA) are tabulated separately from the NOEMA data, providing a clean numeric answer key.
